title: reliability-ops-sync-briefing-sept-10-2026
content:
Reliability Ops Sync — 2026-09-10

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Liam Patel (next on-call), Sofia Alvarez (infra), Jordan Kim (platform), plus ad-hoc: Priya Rao (customer success)

TL;DR:
- Two notable incidents earlier this week drove a small SLO hit. Primary root causes: autoscaler mis-evaluation in a Dedicated GPU pool (INC-2026-09-08) and a stale prefix cache post-deploy that surfaced incorrect completions for some long-lived sessions (INC-2026-09-09).
- Mitigations worked; overall user impact was limited to a subset of enterprise customers but we missed the monthly availability SLO window for the API write route.
- Action items created (see section below) — priority is autoscaler tuning and a deploy-time cache-flush step.

Incident summaries
1) INC-2026-09-08 — GPU pool autoscaler error + transient driver restart
- Time window: 2026-09-08 13:40–14:00 UTC
- Symptom: sudden P95 latency jump (API generation route) and increased 5xxs for ~18 minutes.
- Root cause (initial): autoscaler mis-evaluated burst traffic as sustained and attempted to scale down shortly after scaling up, combined with a GPU driver restart on one node in the dedicated-serving pool. The combination caused a temporary capacity gap while requests were rescheduled.
- Mitigation taken: manual scale-up to 30% above baseline, routed affected traffic to regional fallback pool (eu-west fallback) via smart routing policy, temporarily reverted a recent pod template change. No model-level data corruption.
- Impact: ~4 customer-facing incidents, P95 from baseline ~90ms -> 1.2s at peak, error-rate delta +1.8% during window.
- Follow-up: SRE-521 (postmortem draft), infra ticket to add a safety-window to autoscaler decision logic (owner: Sofia, due 2026-09-17).

2) INC-2026-09-09 — stale prefix cache leading to incorrect completions
- Time window: 2026-09-09 02:10–03:05 UTC (rolling)
- Symptom: handful of low-volume enterprise customers reported hallucinated completions referencing stale session context.
- Root cause: deploy pipeline changed cache invalidation hook timing; long-lived sessions kept a KV/prefix cache that wasn't invalidated on the model micro-shift (minor variant upgrade).
- Mitigation: coordinated cache flush, hotfix to deploy pipeline to force immediate cache invalidation for active sessions, issued status update to affected customers.
- Impact: 3 enterprise customers saw degraded quality. SLA credit discussion in CS.
- Follow-up: add deploy-time automated cache flush and unit tests in pipeline (owner: Jordan, due 2026-09-14).

SLO snapshot (rolling week ending 2026-09-10)
- Availability (api-v1/write): 99.92% (target 99.95) — MISS for week window
- Error rate (5xx overall): 0.25% (target <0.20%) — small miss
- Latency P95 (generation): 112ms (target 120ms) — OK
- Notes: Availability miss driven primarily by INC-2026-09-08; cross-check billing/commit implications for affected enterprise customers (Priya/CX leading).

Operational handoff notes (for Liam Patel who starts on-call 2026-09-11 09:00 UTC)
- Current on-call owner: Maya Chen (ends 2026-09-11 08:45 UTC).
- Outstanding tickets to watch: SRE-521 (postmortem), INFRA-934 (autoscaler safety window), PLAT-778 (deploy cache flush).
- Known flapping service: dedicated-serving-pool-3 — restart frequency observed after driver patch; avoid rolling restarts until INFRA-934 applied.
- Pager escalation: Pager -> first line eng-sre -> lead-sre -> platform-eng if hardware. Reminder: use the eu fallback routing toggle (console -> routing -> fallback-policy) if latency surge > 500ms for >5m.

Action items (owner, due)
- Sofia: implement autoscaler hysteresis and safety-window; add simulation tests (due 2026-09-17).
- Jordan: add deploy-step to force KV/prefix cache flush for variant rollouts; add pipeline unit test (due 2026-09-14).
- Maya: finalize postmortem draft for SRE-521 and publish to Confluence (due 2026-09-13).
- Priya/CS: customer outreach summary and SLA credit proposal for affected accounts (due 2026-09-12).
- Liam (on-call): validate fallback routing playbook during first 24h of shift and confirm runbook changes are discoverable from Slack (due 2026-09-12).

Metrics notes and dashboard tasks
- Add a short-term dashboard to correlate autoscaler decisions (scale events) against P95 latency with 1m granularity. (Owner: Observability team, request ticket OBS-211 created.)
- Retention: extend SLO event retention to 90 days for easier root cause correlation across deploy windows.

Runbook / playbook updates needed
- Update "model-variant-rollout" runbook to include cache invalidation step (Confluence: runbooks/reliability-playbook).
- Add a runbook section for dedicated pool driver restarts and safe mitigation steps.

Parking lot / unresolved questions
- Should we implement an automated temporary model-variant fallback when autoscaler detects rapid capacity churn? Pros/cons and cost trade-off to be discussed with product. (Tentative meeting: 2026-09-16)
- SLA credits: threshold for automated credits vs manual review — Priya to propose thresholds.

Misc notes / quick wins
- Short term: add a CI smoke test that verifies cache invalidation hook on deploys.
- Medium term: add simulated burst testing to the autoscaler CI pipeline.

If anything urgent pops while I'm handing off, ping me directly in Slack @maya.c (I'll be responsive until 09:00 UTC on 2026-09-11).

End of briefing.
